title: Module 8 Assessment: Production Operations, Upgrades & Lifecycle

questions.prompt: Which Juju command updates a deployed application to a newer charm revision or different channel track?
questions.explanation: 'juju refresh <application>' downloads and applies the new charm revision or channel.

questions.prompt: Which lifecycle hook is dispatched first when a charm revision is refreshed on a unit?
questions.explanation: The 'upgrade-charm' hook runs immediately upon unpacking the new charm code.

questions.prompt: How do coordinated production charms perform zero-downtime upgrades across clustered units?
options: By orchestrating rolling upgrades across peer relations and failing over primary leadership sequentially
By terminating all units simultaneously and restarting the entire cluster
By deploying duplicate controllers in round-robin fashion
By pausing all network traffic at the Linux kernel firewall
questions.answer: By orchestrating rolling upgrades across peer relations and failing over primary leadership sequentially
questions.explanation: Production charms use peer relations and leader coordination to upgrade secondary units before switching leadership.

questions.prompt: What command prepares a machine for an operating system series upgrade (e.g. Ubuntu 20.04 to 22.04)?
questions.explanation: 'juju upgrade-machine prepare' instructs charms to prepare state before the host OS upgrade runs.

questions.prompt: Which Juju command archives the controller's internal database, credentials, and state for disaster recovery?
questions.explanation: 'juju create-backup' creates a full disaster-recovery archive (.tar.gz) of the controller state.

questions.prompt: What is the primary benefit of 'juju migrate <model> <target-controller>'?
options: It transfers live running workloads and agent connections to a new controller without downtime
It converts machine charms to Kubernetes sidecar charms
It compresses all log files on the target machine into gzip archives
It deletes all persistent volumes attached to units
questions.answer: It transfers live running workloads and agent connections to a new controller without downtime
questions.explanation: 'juju migrate' re-homes unit and machine agents to a target controller while workloads remain running.

questions.prompt: Which command exports the live topology, scale, and relations of a model into a reusable YAML bundle?
questions.explanation: 'juju export-bundle' generates a declarative bundle YAML file from the active model.

questions.prompt: How does the Canonical Observability Stack (COS) collect metrics and system logs from machine workloads?
options: Via the grafana-agent subordinate charm related with the cos-agent interface
By running continuous SSH scrapers from the controller
By broadcasting syslog packets over UDP port 514
Through daily cron jobs that rsync /var/log to NFS
questions.answer: Via the grafana-agent subordinate charm related with the cos-agent interface
questions.explanation: The 'grafana-agent' subordinate charm scrapes metrics and logs locally and ships them to COS via CMR.

questions.prompt: What model configuration key dynamically controls logging verbosity across Juju subsystems?
questions.explanation: 'juju model-config logging-config="..."' allows tuning root, unit, and uniter log verbosity dynamically.

questions.prompt: Which command is used to retry a failed charm hook after fixing an environmental error?
questions.explanation: 'juju resolved <unit> --retry' instructs Juju to re-dispatch the failed hook.
